code_label: MIS as antenna placement optimization
text_span: the optimal choice of antenna placements corresponds to a maximum independent set on a unit disk graph
rationale: Gives the first concrete application example.

code_label: FM radio station spacing as MIS
text_span: allowed configurations of FM radio stations correspond to an independent set in a quasi-2D geometry
rationale: Identifies a real-world regulatory application of MIS.

code_label: MIS appears in many other applications
text_span: There are many other applications of MIS.
rationale: Signals the breadth of the problem class across domains.

code_label: Portfolio optimization via maximum clique
text_span: Portfolio optimization is one of the interesting applications of the maximum clique problem [19, 23].
rationale: Introduces a finance-related application.

code_label: Clique and independent set are complements
text_span: the MIS vertex set I of a graph G is equivalent to the maximum clique of the complement graph G, and vice versa.
rationale: States the reduction used to connect two problem classes.

code_label: Molecular docking can be cast as maximum clique
text_span: Every maximal clique of G corresponds to a maximal matching between protein points P and ligand points S.
rationale: Describes the combinatorial formulation of docking.

code_label: Vertex cover complements MIS
text_span: the maximum independent set and minimum vertex cover are complementary problems
rationale: States the relationship used to solve vertex cover via MIS.

code_label: Network immunization as minimum vertex cover
text_span: The goal is to then intelligently select nodes so that the spread is completely cut, while the resources required are minimized.
rationale: Summarizes the optimization objective in the immunization example.

code_label: Dominating set requires every node to be covered
text_span: a dominating set is a subset of vertices D ⊆V of a graph G that has the property that every vertex in G is either in D, or adjacent to a vertex in D.
rationale: Defines the problem class for the 5G example.

code_label: Dominating sets are handled in hybrid mode
text_span: this is not the case for dominating sets.
rationale: States that the ground-state encoding does not directly apply.

code_label: Hybrid sampling and post-processing for dominating sets
text_span: the neutral-atom device can, for example, work in a sampling mode, providing independent sets from some weighted probability distribution
rationale: Describes the proposed workaround for a non-native objective.

code_label: Connected dominating sets are not directly independent sets
text_span: the MCDS problem does not directly fall into the class of independent set problems.
rationale: Explicitly notes the mismatch with the native problem class.

code_label: Approximation factor for connected dominating sets
text_span: it is possible to find a connected dominating set within a factor of three of the MCDS.
rationale: Reports an approximation guarantee used in the discussion.

code_label: Ad-hoc routing as connected dominating set
text_span: One application of connected dominating sets to ad-hoc networks is for routing protocols
rationale: Introduces the networking application example.

code_label: Counting independent sets is #P-complete
text_span: computing the number of independent sets is a #P-complete (pronounced sharp P complete) counting problem [6].
rationale: States the computational hardness of the counting task.

code_label: Partition functions and expectations are hard
text_span: computing expectation values is typically hard as well.
rationale: Extends the hardness claim to statistical quantities.

code_label: Loss networks use route interaction graphs
text_span: The size of the maximum independent set is thus the largest number of possible simultaneous phone calls on the network.
rationale: Connects the counting model to telecommunications capacity.

code_label: Quantum sampling can reproduce weighted distributions
text_span: A quantum state can be constructed adiabatically or variationally [14] that could reproduce this probability distribution
rationale: Describes the proposed quantum sampling approach.

code_label: Maximal independent sets support incremental planning
text_span: computing statistics of weighted ensembles of maximal independent sets may be useful for incremental store placement.
rationale: Introduces the planning application under uncertainty.

code_label: Sampling maximal independent sets is hard
text_span: sampling from a weighted distribution of independent sets, or counting the number of maximal independent sets, is hard.
rationale: States a computational challenge motivating the method.

code_label: Quantum-sampled MIS can seed classical post-processing
text_span: the neutral-atom device can be used in a sampling mode to solve the incremental store placement problem using classical post-processing and quantum machine learning
rationale: Describes the hybrid workflow for the store-placement example.

code_label: Graph coloring reduces to independent set
text_span: graph K-coloring has an extremely natural reduction to the independent set problem
rationale: States the reduction used for scheduling.

code_label: Scheduling maximizes asset utilization
text_span: The goal is to find a schedule of tasks that maximize asset utilization by minimizing the number of rounds.
rationale: Summarizes the optimization objective in the scheduling example.

code_label: Reductions and mappings extend beyond independent set
text_span: Other hard combinatorial optimization problems can be solved using solutions from maximum independent set problems using reductions and mappings.
locator: XIV. Solving problems beyond independent set using reductions and mappings
rationale: States the paper’s broader methodological claim.

code_label: SAT can be mapped to independent set
text_span: the equation is satisfiable if the independent set size is equal to the number of clauses.
locator: XIV. Solving problems beyond independent set using reductions and mappings
rationale: Gives a specific reduction example beyond the core problem class.

code_label: QUBO can be encoded in weighted independent set
text_span: By choosing weights of a unit disk graph, the optimal bitstring xi is encoded in the maximum weighted independent set
locator: XIV. Solving problems beyond independent set using reductions and mappings
rationale: Describes another mapping from a general optimization problem.
